questions.stem_text:
Which of the following is the symplastic pathway for the movement of sucrose from the site
of photosynthesis in mesophyll cells into the phloem?

options.A: Bundle sheath, companion cell, phloem parenchyma, fibers
options.B: Phloem parenchyma, bundle sheath, fibers, companion cell
options.C: Bundle sheath, phloem parenchyma, companion cell, sieve tube
options.D: Bundle sheath, fibers, companion cell, sieve tube
options.E: Fibers, bundle sheath, companion cell, sieve tube

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - Bundle sheath, phloem parenchyma, companion cell, sieve tube

questions.stem_text: What prevents the stomach from being digested by itsown secretions?

options.A: The thick muscular wall of the stomach
options.D: High pH levels in the stomach

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - The thick muscular wall of the stomach

questions.stem_text: What is the physiological purpose of shivering?

options.A: Shivering is a method the body uses to relieve pain.
options.B: Shivering is a tactic to ward off predators by appearing agitated.
options.C: Shivering is a way to burn excess calories
options.D: Shivering is a response to fear or anxiety
options.E: Shivering is an involuntary action to prepare muscles for physical activity.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - Shivering is a method the body uses to relieve pain.

questions.stem_text: What are some of the cues used by animal in migrating?

options.B: Atmospheric oxygen levels, plant growth, tidal patterns
options.C: Infrared radiation, sound frequency, barometric pressure
options.D: Moon phases, echo location, gravitational pull
options.E: Sunlight intensity, water current, soil composition

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - Taste, wind direction, humidity

questions.stem_text:
In certain abnormal conditions, the stomach does not secretehydrochloric acid. What
effects might this haveon thedigestive process?

options.A: Without HCl, more bacteria would be killed in the stomach.
options.B: No HCl would lead to reduced mucus production in the stomach lining.
options.C: The absence of HCl would cause the stomach to digest its own tissues.
options.D: No HCl in the stomach would significantly increase the pH of the small intestine.
options.E: The absence of HCl would speed up the digestive process.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - Without HCl, more bacteria would be killed in the stomach.

questions.stem_text: Does anterior laxity of the uninjured knee influence clinical outcomes of ACL reconstruction?
questions.answer_explanation: Greater anterior laxity of the uninjured knee was associated with poorer stability and functional outcomes after ACL reconstruction. Excessive anterior laxity of the uninjured knee thus appears to represent a risk factor for inferior outcomes.

questions.stem_text: Are UK radiologists satisfied with the training and support received in suspected child abuse?
questions.answer_explanation: The survey shows significant dissatisfaction amongst consultant radiologists with the current service, confirms a low number of paediatric radiologists taking on this work, and suggests the potential to increase numbers of radiology child abuse experts by 27% if given improved training and support. Appropriate service and education strategies should be implemented.

questions.stem_text: Must early postoperative oral intake be limited to laparoscopy?
questions.answer_explanation: Early oral intake is possible after laparotomy and colorectal resection. Thus, the laparoscopic surgeon's claim of early tolerated oral intake may not be unique to laparoscopy.

questions.stem_text: Can the prognosis of polymyalgia rheumatica be predicted at disease onset?
questions.answer_explanation: A higher PV in PMR increases the risk of prolonged steroid therapy and late GCA. Female sex and particular HLA alleles may increase the risk of late GCA. Starting patients on>15 mg prednisolone is associated with a prolonged steroid duration.

questions.stem_text: Thrombosis prophylaxis in hospitalised medical patients: does prophylaxis in all patients make sense?
questions.answer_explanation: The incidence of venous thrombosis during hospitalisation in a department of general internal medicine is low and does not justify prophylaxis in all internal patients. Cancer is a strong risk factor for hospital-acquired thrombosis in the medical ward. Further studies may answer the question as to whether thrombosis prophylaxis in this subgroup is feasible.
